questions.scenario: A VPC Flow Logs record for the app ENI shows destination port 5432 and action REJECT. What does that evidence establish?

options.text: The observed network flow was rejected by an evaluated network control.
The application parsed the database response incorrectly.
The database password is wrong.
Reachability Analyzer changed the route.

questions.explanation: Flow logs record IP traffic metadata and acceptance or rejection. They do not prove application or database authentication behavior. Learn more in [VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html).

questions.scenario: Before a production change, a team wants to know whether current AWS routing and network controls allow a path from an ALB ENI to an ECS task ENI. Which tool statically analyzes that configuration?

options.text: AWS Budgets.
VPC Reachability Analyzer.
CloudWatch RUM.
S3 Inventory.

questions.explanation: Reachability Analyzer models the configured path and identifies blocking components without sending packets. Learn more in [Reachability Analyzer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/what-is-reachability-analyzer.html).

questions.scenario: Only orders tasks in one Availability Zone time out when connecting to a private database, while the same task revision stays healthy in the other Zone. The deployment and application configuration are identical. Which first comparison is most useful?

options.text: Delete every security group and retry.
Move the database to a public subnet.
Compare the affected and healthy task ENIs, subnets, route tables, NACLs, and flow-log records.
Change the Route 53 TTL.

questions.explanation: Comparing the healthy and unhealthy path isolates the AZ-specific difference while preserving evidence. Learn more in [VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html).

questions.scenario: A security group allows the request, but a custom NACL blocks return traffic on ephemeral ports. Which distinction explains the failure?

options.text: Both controls are stateful.
NACLs apply only to IAM calls.
Security groups route packets between VPCs.
Security groups are stateful, while NACLs are stateless and need compatible rules in both directions.

questions.explanation: NACLs are stateless subnet controls, so return traffic must be allowed explicitly. Learn more in [VPC network ACLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html).

questions.scenario: An internal API call times out intermittently and several teams own parts of the path. Which evidence belongs in a repeatable AWS timeout investigation?

options.text: The exact source, destination, protocol, and port.
A guessed fix applied before collecting the failing path.
Route-table associations and longest-prefix route targets.
Change the IAM password policy for human users.
Security group, NACL, and flow-log evidence.

questions.explanation: A concrete flow definition plus route and policy evidence makes the investigation reproducible and keeps guesses from destroying useful state. Learn more in [Reachability Analyzer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/reachability/what-is-reachability-analyzer.html) and [VPC Flow Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html).
